clue.text: Spare site — one developed for a food shop

indicators.note: something developed has been worked up into a new form, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unused plot of land is built on to make room for a food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is SPARE SITE plus I; a patisserie is a cake shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a shop selling pastries and cakes, so it is one kind of food retailer.

clue.text: Mail vessels turning tail

indicators.note: turning the tail means the end of the word is switched round, so its last two letters swap places

explanation.surface: Ships carrying the mail turn around and head back.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessels are pots, not ships; only the final pair of letters is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is the British word for letters and parcels delivered, the same as mail.

clue.text: Heard a king within, and lingered

indicators.note: within places the words before it inside the other piece

parts.note: a judge who has heard a case has tried it
A plus R, Latin rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone listened to a king's speech and hung about.
explanation.walkthrough: Heard is used in the court sense: a case heard is a case tried.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to stay longer than intended or delay leaving, so tarried means lingered.

clue.text: Foreign money found among loose coins, as in the city

indicators.note: found among says one piece sits in the middle of the others
loose means not held in order, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: the franc was the French currency

explanation.surface: A traveller finds some foreign currency among the loose change in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: San Francisco is the Californian city on its famous bay, so it is the city meant.

clue.text: Give power to the right soldiers in various directions

indicators.note: in places the words before it inside the following piece

explanation.surface: Troops on the right are empowered to move off in several directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill something with energy or put electric current through it.

clue.text: Popular young man having one of these nightmares

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in cub reporter

explanation.surface: A well-liked young chap suffers one of these bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Incubi are demons once thought to lie on sleepers, hence nightmares.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an oppressive demon of folklore and so, by extension, a nightmare or crushing burden.

clue.text: After a short time, succeeded as a bookmaker

indicators.note: after says the following piece comes later in the answer than the one it is after

parts.note: A plus MO, a moment or short time
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone takes up bookmaking soon after starting out, as at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The bookmaker is not a betting man but the prophet AMOS, who gave his name to (made) a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The prophet Amos is credited with the Old Testament book bearing his name, so he is jokingly its maker.

clue.text: Sienese painter carrying his work in a car?

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An Italian painter drives his canvas around in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'a car' is a particular make, the Mini.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone Martini was a fourteenth-century Gothic master of the Siena school of painting.

clue.text: Little sibling, about ten, with whistle and gun

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: a hooter is a whistle or siren

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old little sister gets a whistle and a toy gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Little sibling means a short form of the word, not a younger sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver holding six rounds, the classic gun of the Wild West.

clue.text: Rigger, say, using cord in Parisian style — extremely chancy

indicators.note: extremely points to just the outermost ends of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters of chancy

explanation.surface: A rigger works with cords in a French manner, which sounds extremely risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigger, say' is the definition by sound: rigger is said like rigour, and rigour is stringency. Extremely takes only the ends of chancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringency is strictness or severity, which is what rigour means, and rigour is pronounced just like rigger.

clue.text: Grain mostly eaten by animal, an antelope

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
what is eaten by something ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
rye, a cereal grain, without its last letter

explanation.surface: An animal munches most of the grain put out; the creature in question is an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large straight-horned antelope of African and Arabian deserts.

clue.text: With determination, new peers can interject at any time

indicators.note: to interject is to throw something in between, so a piece is placed inside
new means made afresh, so the letters following are put in another order

explanation.surface: Newly ennobled lords are determined to butt into debates whenever they like.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseverance is persistence in a course of action despite difficulty, steady determination.

clue.text: Mole takes food beside river

indicators.note: beside places one piece directly next to the other in the answer

parts.note: a pie is a dish of food
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A burrowing mole helps itself to a meal down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole is not the animal but a stone breakwater or jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive stone structure built out into the sea as a breakwater or landing stage, like a jetty.

clue.text: Incomprehensible sounds of the Rock King, included in error

parts.note: Gib is the short name for Gibraltar, the Rock

indicators.note: something included in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: Odd noises come from a king on Gibraltar, caught up in some mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rock is Gibraltar; bish is British slang for a mistake, and ER (Edward Rex) can stand for a king as well as a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish is meaningless or unintelligible talk, noises that make no sense to the hearer.

clue.text: Money inadequate at first for cake

indicators.note: at first says the piece it follows is to be put at the start of the answer

explanation.surface: Without enough cash to start with, someone can't afford a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The money comes first in the clue but last in the answer, as at first instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a rich buttery biscuit, often baked as a round slab like a flat cake.

clue.text: Male head of department is not, perhaps, a pleasure-seeker

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
perhaps hints the words before it are only one possible arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A department's male boss is perhaps not someone who lives for pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedonist is someone whose chief aim in life is enjoyment and sensual gratification.

clue.text: Northerner first to enter, thus embracing O'Hara

indicators.note: first to signals taking only the opening letter of the next word
to embrace is to hold something within one's arms, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: so means thus or in this way
Kim O'Hara is the boy hero of Kipling's novel Kim

explanation.surface: A northern visitor goes in first and hugs someone called O'Hara.
explanation.walkthrough: O'Hara is the surname of Kipling's Kim, so it stands for that first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskimo is an older name for the Inuit and related peoples of the Arctic far north.

clue.text: A girl's initially on edge, perhaps, in the sultan's palace

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters are only one possible arrangement
initially means taking the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the first letters of on and edge

explanation.surface: A young woman is nervous and jumpy inside the sultan's palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Muslim palace, and by extension the sultan's palace itself.

clue.text: Castle that is identified by a raw recruit

parts.note: the rook is the chess piece also called a castle
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A castle is pointed out to a new and untrained army recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, originally army slang for an inexperienced new soldier.

clue.text: Vehicle taking people to the works together

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old full name of the bus
second meaning: a volume collecting an author's writings

explanation.surface: A bus ferries the staff to the factory as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: The works sounds like a factory, but it means an author's writings gathered in one volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is both the original name for a bus and a single volume reprinting several works.

clue.text: Wilful priest rejected in a Cambridge school

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the following one

parts.note: the Perse School is a long-established school in Cambridge

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Rev, short for reverend, a title of the clergy

explanation.surface: A headstrong clergyman is turned away from a Cambridge school.
explanation.walkthrough: The Perse is an independent school in Cambridge, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means deliberately contrary and stubborn, insisting on behaving unreasonably, much as wilful does.

clue.text: Odious type identified by raised hat

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A nasty character is recognised by the hat he lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised seems to describe the hat, but it acts on 'by' just before it; tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptile is used figuratively for a contemptible, sly or grovelling person.

clue.text: Hired mourner is outside in a very short time

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping round it, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: a mute was a paid attendant at a funeral

explanation.surface: A paid mourner stands outside, lingering only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: A mute was a professional mourner hired to attend Victorian funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds, and loosely any brief moment.

clue.text: A single feature in a bachelor's porcelain

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the word that follows

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A lone eye-catching item sits in a single man's china cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: A bachelor here is the graduate with a BA, not an unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine translucent porcelain made with bone ash in the clay.

clue.text: Fully developed variety of 12

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different version of it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jetty, in another form, has reached full maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to the answer of 12 across, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe describes fruit or anything else that has matured completely and is ready.

clue.text: Bird known for its song — or talk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a songbird such as the stonechat or whinchat

explanation.walkthrough: The bird is named for its chattering call, which links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Chats are small songbirds of the thrush family, and to chat is to talk casually.

clue.text: The accomplished retire to this island

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Skilled and successful people go into retirement on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon, a most accomplished man, was exiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an island off the Tuscan coast of Italy, famous as Napoleon's first place of exile.

clue.text: Like an unconventional lout — also his bizarre appearance

definitions.text: Like an unconventional lout — also his bizarre appearance

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual form, so the letters of the next word are reordered
bizarre means strange and out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball yob looks as strange as he behaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a lout who is unconventional, with bizarre looks, is outlandish.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strikingly strange or unfamiliar, describing both unconventional behaviour and a weird look.

clue.text: Daughter approaching river in partial darkness

indicators.note: approaching places the first piece right up next to the following one

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: A girl walks towards the river as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The Usk is a river in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim time of evening twilight, when light is fading but not yet gone.

clue.text: Eastern people involved in study? Unfashionable resolution

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it, so the pieces go within

parts.note: a den is a private study
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Easterners caught up in their studies resolve things in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the break between study and the rest; the resolution is the unravelling at a story's end.
explanation.definitionFit: A denouement is the final resolution of a plot, where the strands of a story are untangled.
